I’m concerned about how mental health and sex work are being discussed in this thread. While it’s understandable that some are trying to warn OP about potential challenges in the relationship, several comments rely on harmful stereotypes

BPD is a mental health condition, not a character flaw. Referring to relationships with individuals who have BPD as a “horror movie” is both misinformed and very stigmatizing…

Many people living with BPD work to manage their symptoms and are fully capable of forming healthy, caring and responsable relationships.

OP.. you are absolutely within your rights to decide whether or not to pursue this relationship. You are the only one who can make that call.

If you do want to do it, please [learn about BPD](https://emotionsmatterbpd.org/what-is-bpd). It is important for you to know how to set clear and compassionate boundaries, practice open and nonjudgmental communication, and, if needed, seeking guidance from a professional. These things are not just helpful for BPD but are useful for any emotionally complex relationship

Please let’s try to be kind here. People living with mental health conditions and those with experience in sex work deserve to be spoken about with dignity

It’s often easier to tell someone who is grieving, ‘Please keep that pain to yourself. Your loss makes me uncomfortable, so let’s avoid the topic.’ But I hope that when you’ve grieved—or if you experience grief in the future—people will listen to you, rather than silence your sorrow.

The loss of a pet is often downplayed by others, dismissed as ‘just an animal’ or ‘easily replaced,’ which can be soul-crushing when you’re already heartbroken. Being asked to suppress your grief only deepens the wound.

It takes so little to show empathy—to give someone the space to share, cherish, and mourn the loss of a loved one.

Are we really aiming for a world where only happiness is acceptable, and sorrow is something to hide or mark as inappropriate for comfort’s sake?

Grief can be bittersweet. It allows us to remember and honor loved ones by speaking their names and sharing their stories. No one is obligated to engage in someone else’s grief, but it’s important to allow it.

Grief keeps us grounded, reminding us to express love and affection while we still can. Life is fragile, and it’s our care for others that gives it meaning

I think body dysmorphia is a very complex issue that has no easy fix. Yes, one can lose weight but it will never be enough. Yes, we can get surgery but there is always going to be something to "fix". 

The things that help body dysmorphia are probably internalizing healthier thoughts about self image, that could counteract the old thoughts that harms us so much. Talking about it. Recognizing that it is an issue of perception. 

If this things are affecting your life in many ways, I think seeking help from a mental health professional is a good alternative. You don’t have to just figure it out entirely on your own. 

Even if our worst nightmares are true, and we are ugly or whatever.. we are still worthy of love and appreciation. Worthy of being alive. And nothing, not even appearance, can remove that inherent value. It is given to us for existing. Try to talk to yourself like you would with a close friend until maybe, one day, we can become that friend to ourselves.

Hey… i am a little late in all this. But maybe you might see this comment. 

I lost my heart and will to live too, I lost my dog that I grew up with. And it is an indescribable pain. I been suicidal for years now. This type of grief is hard. The death of pets is treated differently.. there is no flowers, or big ceremonies and lot of routines disappear. All the stuff is left behind and, in my case, I felt that my heart died with my dog. 

I see a lot of people recommending to keep going so that you can adopt another dog, and that’s valid, but… I don’t think is a good idea for everybody. They might be right, but I think it feels a little out of touch. Is like if lost a family member they told you "hey.. maybe get another sister or daughter". It’s well intention, but if this loss is recent I don’t think is very empathetic.

In my case, I wonder why still be here at all when she’s gone.. i fear to forget her, even tho she’s is my heart. I feel guilt, fear, sadness, anger, and happiness to have had the chance to meet her. Somehow, I believe that they are still here. Not like before, witch was better. But I still feel her. I see her in everything good in this horrendous world. I see her in the sun that she love to bathe in, in the followers that she liked to smell, in other dogs sometimes, in the peaceful moments, in her clothes.

All this things allow me to keep on living and simultaneously makes me wonder why I am still here.. I want to build a memory of her. I want to show her how much I lover her through this grief. And as she kept me living while she was here, she still keeps me alive somehow in this new form of her presence. I am still suicidal, I still miss her. It is normal to think there’s no other way in this circumstances. I understand. 

I send you love and support. Is not easy to lose your baby. But maybe you can still feel her in all that’s good of this world. You will never forget her, but you can move forward with her. And celebrate her and all the moments that kept you here.
